lead: West Palm Beach plumbing deals with hurricanes, a high water table and 1920s homes with aging cast-iron drains. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across West Palm Beach.
risk: cast-iron drain failures, storm flooding and slab leaks
risk_short: old drains, flooding and slab leaks
why: El Cid, Flamingo Park, Northwood and Grandview Heights have homes from the 1920s to the 1950s with galvanized supply lines and cast-iron drains. Many mid-century homes have cast-iron drains under the slab.
Hurricanes and heavy rain flood low streets and back up drains. Downtown condos share risers and stacks.
utility: City of West Palm Beach Public Utilities
water: West Palm Beach draws its water from Clear Lake, fed by the Grassy Waters Preserve wetland. Algae in the source water is monitored, and the city posts water quality notices.
tips: Have cast-iron drains scoped in older homes.
Shut off the main valve before a hurricane evacuation.
Check historic district rules before exterior work.
Sign up for city water notices.
areas: PipeMend works in El Cid, Flamingo Park, Northwood, Grandview Heights, SoSo, Downtown and every other West Palm Beach neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of West Palm Beach Building Division, and plumbing contractors are licensed by the Florida Construction Industry Licensing Board.

faq.q: Where does West Palm Beach get its water?
faq.a: From Clear Lake, which is fed by the Grassy Waters Preserve, a protected wetland west of the city. Unlike most South Florida cities, it relies mainly on surface water.
